annotationRationale: Parity, or congruence modulo 2, forces a unique all-odd row and column. Combinations count the equally likely parity patterns, and the multiplication principle counts the nine favorable patterns.
sourceMethod: Follows the official parity-pattern argument, adding explicit justification that the nine patterns are exhaustive, distinct, and equally likely.

review.mathCheck: Five odd entries force row odd-counts 3,1,1 and column odd-counts 3,1,1. Their unique all-odd row and column occupy exactly five squares. There are 9 such patterns among C(9,4)=126 equally likely parity patterns, giving 1/14, choice B.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, independently worded adaptation of official #20 on pp.11-12. It retains the all-odd row/column count and strengthens the explanation with sufficiency, uniqueness, and equal-likelihood justifications.
review.annotationCheck: All favorable configurations are characterized, duplicate counting is excluded, and the 4!5! multiplicity justifies the sample space. The explanation is complete at AMC 12 level.
